text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The direct talks scheduled to start on July 9 between President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash will be in phases and are expected to last some time.
- The attorney-general describes the situation concerning organised crime in Cyprus as worrying.
- The government plans to enact legislation empowering the interior ministry to close establishments which violate the terms of their building permits.
- Communist Akel party chief Demetris Christofias: It is the order of the people to get rid of the current right-wing government in the forthcoming presidential elections.
- A convict jailed for burglary was given a presidential pardon last week for his involvement in anti-occupation activitites.

- The United Nations will not set an agenda in the forthcoming direct talks so there is flexibility in discussions. The Greek side is expected to raise security issues and the Turkish side constitutional aspects of the Cyprus problem.
- A 37-year-old man is being held by the occupation army. He entered the north on Sunday morning and witnesses saw Turkish soldiers beat him.

- Labour partners call a temporary truce on outstanding issues relating to the renewal of collective working agreements for some 130,000 employees, waiting until after the presidential elections in February to take up the issue again.

- During the direct talks in July Clerides will ask Denktash to show a conciliatory stand on the basic aspects of the Cyprus issue, which are territorial issues, basic freedoms, political equality, sovereignty and security, according to Foreign Minister Yiannakis Cassoulides.
- The Attorney-General's office will make suggestions to police on ways to intensify their efforts to clamp down on organised crime.
